answer_1.quote: We have selected two well-studied tasks from the literature: knowledge‑grounded dialogue and abstractive summarization...

answer_2.quote: We used various evaluation metrics applied for knowledge grounding and natural language generation. For token‑based automatic metrics, we used BLEU‑4, Rouge‑L, ChrF, and METEOR... For knowledge‑based metrics, we first used Knowledge‑F1 (KF1)... We also utilize UniEval... we also employ MFMA...

answer_4.quote: We also conducted a human evaluation of the generated responses to assess their quality. We randomly sampled 100 examples and asked 3 different evaluators to measure their fluency, relevance to the dialogue context, groundedness to reference knowledge, and if the response is an unnatural copy of the knowledge...
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators were asked to rate each generated output on fluency, relevance (to dialogue context or article), groundedness to the provided knowledge, and whether it is an unnatural copy (for dialogue) or completeness (for summarization).
